versions.label: 1976 map
versions.long: Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976, as amended
sources: Numbers, names, Lok Sabha seats: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2004, Vol. III (Assembly segments)
Reservations: the pre-2008 map file (T3); totals checked against the 2008 Order, Schedule II
AC shapes: ECI via DataMeet (india-geodata eci-statewise), placed on the map by a fitted transform; median error 0.22 km
PC shapes: merged from the AC shapes
notes: Seat numbers, names and Lok Sabha seats are those in force before 2008, as ECI's report on the 2004 Lok Sabha election lists them. Assembly reservations come from the pre-2008 map file; their totals equal the 2008 Order's Schedule II.

The pre-2008 map was placed on the ground by a fitted transform (median distance from the state's 2008 outline 0.22 km), then fitted to the state's outer boundary, which did not change in 2008; gaps along the edge went to the neighbouring seat.

caution.reason: Small seat (under 60 km²): a placing error of a few hundred metres is a large share of it, so a place near its edge may belong to the neighbouring seat. City seats are the least reliable (in Bombay the source map had to be redrawn).

versions.label: 1976 map
versions.long: Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976, as amended
versions.used: in force until 2023 (Assam was left out of the 2008 Order)
sources: Numbers, names, Lok Sabha seats: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2004, Vol. III (Assembly segments)
Reservations: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2009; totals checked against the 2008 Order, Schedule II
AC shapes: DataMeet India_AC (T3), whose Assam layer is the 1976 map; PCs merged from them with ECI's lists
notes: Assam was left out of the 2008 Order (Delimitation Act 2002, section 10A), so it voted on the 1976 map until 2021.

Seat numbers, names and Lok Sabha seats as ECI's report on the 2004 Lok Sabha election lists them; Assembly reservations from ECI's 2009 report (the same map). Their totals equal the 2008 Order's Schedule II.

versions.label: 2023 map
versions.long: Delimitation of Assam by the Election Commission of India, Orders No. 1 (20 June 2023) and No. 2 (11 August 2023)
sources: AC shapes, numbers, names: ECI's results-portal map of the 2026 Assam Assembly election (T2, via the Internet Archive)
Reservations, Lok Sabha seats, districts: Srinivas Kodali, Assam delimitation layer (T3, CC BY 4.0), checked against ECI's 2024 Lok Sabha map
In force: Gazette of India, S.O. 3661(E), 16 August 2023 (T1)
notes: The Election Commission redrew Assam's seats in 2023 on the 2001 Census (Representation of the People Act 1950, section 8A), keeping 126 Assembly and 14 Lok Sabha seats; the President set 16 August 2023 as the date the Orders took effect (Gazette of India, S.O. 3661(E)).

Seat numbers and names come from ECI's own map of the 2026 Assembly results; reservations and Lok Sabha seats from Srinivas Kodali's layer, digitised from the Commission's maps, whose numbers and names agree with ECI's for all 126 seats. The Orders' own schedules have not been located; the totals (9 SC and 19 ST Assembly seats, 1 SC and 2 ST Lok Sabha seats) are those reported for the final Order.

versions.label: Before 2022
versions.long: Assembly seats of the 1995 delimitation of the state of Jammu and Kashmir; Lok Sabha seats of the 1976 Order
sources: Numbers, names, Lok Sabha seats: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2004, Vol. III (Assembly segments)
Reservations: ECI, Statistical Report on the General Elections 2009 (7 SC)
AC shapes: DataMeet India_AC (T3); PCs merged from them with ECI's lists
notes: Jammu and Kashmir was outside the Delimitation Act 2002. Its 87 Assembly seats (Ladakh's four included) came from the state's own 1995 delimitation; its six Lok Sabha seats from the 1976 Order.

Parts of the former state administered by Pakistan or China are not divided into constituencies on either map. The source map's seats reach past the Line of Control in places and miss some ground the 2022 map covers, so they are fitted to the ground the 2022 seats cover, plus Ladakh (1,332 km² of them left out, 2,108 km² given to the neighbouring seat), and both maps cover the same places.

versions.label: 2022 map
versions.long: Jammu and Kashmir Delimitation Commission, Orders O.N. 6(E) (14 March 2022) and O.N. 17(E) (5 May 2022)
sources: AC shapes, numbers, names: ECI's results-portal map of the 2024 J&K Assembly election (T2, via the Internet Archive)
Reservations, districts, Lok Sabha seats: shijithpk/2024_maps_supplement (T3, Unlicense), checked against ECI's names
Ladakh: the old map's Ladakh seat (DataMeet India_AC), minus the new J&K seats
notes: The Commission drew 90 Assembly seats (43 in the Jammu division, 47 in the Kashmir division; 7 SC, 9 ST) and five Lok Sabha seats of 18 Assembly seats each for the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.

Ladakh, a Union territory without an Assembly since 2019, kept its one Lok Sabha seat, which was not redrawn; it is drawn on the old Ladakh seat's ground and numbered 6 here (ECI numbers it 1 in Ladakh).

Seat numbers and names come from ECI's own map of the 2024 J&K Assembly results; reservations, districts and Lok Sabha seats from an open layer made from the official maps. The Orders' own schedules have not been located; the totals are those reported for the final Order.
Parts of the former state administered by Pakistan or China are not divided into constituencies on either map.

versions.label: 1976 map
versions.long: Delimitation of Parliamentary and Assembly Constituencies Order, 1976
sources: Order text: ECI archive copy of the 1976 Order, Schedule XIII (scan)
AC shapes: ECI via DataMeet (india-geodata eci-statewise), placed on the map by a fitted transform; typical error about 0.5 km
City seats: redrawn from the Order's ward lists (located on OpenStreetMap) where that fits the 2004 electors better; About lists which
PC shapes: merged from the AC shapes; Bombay's outer edge from the 1976 PC file (same source)
versions.short_note: 1976 lines are approximate (about 0.5 km); Bombay and Nagpur city seats redrawn from the Order's ward lists; 2 Assembly seats not drawn
versions.res_note: Shown as {res}, as in force before 2008 (the seat totals then match the 2008 Order's Schedule II). The 1976 Order as printed in the ECI archive copy lists this seat as {printed}: the change came by a later amendment, not yet located.
notes: Reservations on this map are those in force before 2008. Their totals match the 2008 Order's Schedule II (Assembly 18 SC, 22 ST; Lok Sabha 3 SC, 4 ST). The 1976 Order as printed (ECI archive copy) reserves 17 SC and 17 ST Assembly seats and 3 SC and 3 ST Lok Sabha seats: Palghar, Baglan, Nandurbar, Gadchiroli and Kelapur (ST), Kallam (SC) and the Dhulia Lok Sabha seat (ST) were reserved by a later amendment.
Names are as printed in the 1976 Order; the spelling ECI used later is in brackets (Poona, later Pune).

The 1976 Assembly map was placed on the ground by a fitted transform (typical error about 0.5 km, several km in places) and then fitted to the state's outer boundary, which did not change in 2008; gaps along the edge went to the neighbouring seat.

hide.reason: Bombay and Nagpur 1976 Assembly seats are redrawn from the Order's ward lists, which fit the 2004 electors better than the source map. 2 seats (23 Opera House, 48 Nehru Nagar) are not drawn: none of their wards could be placed.

caution.reason: Nagpur and Poona city seats: these lines and an independent rebuild from the Order's ward lists put about half of the city's hexagons in different seats, so a place here may belong to the neighbouring 1976 seat.

from_file.reason: The 1976 PC file gives only the outer edge of PCs 4 to 9; inside it, the Assembly seats and their Lok Sabha seats come from the Order's ward lists and AC lists.
